Bhí clog sa chill is níor bhinn clog é..

<< Had fierce Garbh Doire heard the sound of a bell in this western chapel,
he would have soon gone in and broken the clerics bell.
Had Fionn, the warrior, heard the sound of thy little bell,
Cleric, he would assuredly have gone to meet you
and you would not have been able to escape.
Had Conan of the Fiana heard the note of this bell
that comes to me from the west,
though all the clerics of the world had been present
they would all have been dead.
Had dear Caoilte heard it,
a man who did not refuse battle,
he would have gone in, no lie, and broken your little bells.
I am Oisin, Fionn’s good son: I believe in the God above, 0 Tailgeann.
Though tonight I am without the Fian,
without wealth, the bell’s note gives me pain.>>

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on April 20th, 2010.

The Chapel Bell, X:14

From the playing of The Navigators.

On their record they play the last bunch of notes in each part an octave lower (more like the regular setting), as “BAF | GFD EGA” or “BAF | GFD E3”. Live they play it the octave higher, which is an interesting variation from other settings.

They also play a B-note after that long f-note in the B Part, which I’ve changed to a d-note by preference.

The Chapel Bell, X:19

This is what I hear on the Carlos Sweeney, McCartin recording. I think the flute and fiddle are often doing slightly different triplets.
I LOVE the idea of “B2f ~e3” as a great articulation trick for flute players.
Haven’t heard it before and its easier than the generic “Bee ~e3”
There’s also a weird coloured note in one of the last bars, haven’t figured that out.
Pat

Correctly named?

In Frank McCollam’s (correct spelling) book of his own compositions, this tune appears in the key of D, and is named “The Granny Rock”, after an outcrop at the seafront of his native Ballycastle, Co. Antrim. I believe that the book did not have a huge print run, and I simply have selected photocopies from it. I would be interested to hear, from anyone with a full copy, whether the tune which he wrote and named “The Chapel Bell” is this same tune but in Em, or whether it is an altogether different melody.

The book itself has mysteriously vanished from the local library’s catalogue.

↳ Posted by Jerry O'Donnell on November 7th, 2022.

Re: Correctly Named?

Jerry (Gerry?) O’Donnell is correct about the names of these Frank McCollam jigs. The tune here is The Granny Rock. The Chapel Bell is a different McCollam composition. I’ll post it here when I get the abcs written out. I have the book, given to me by another great Ballycastle fiddler, the late Dominic McNabb.

↳ Posted by seanquinn on September 30th, 2024.

Re: The Original Chapel Bell by Frank McCollam

Here is an abc transcription of THE CHAPEL BELL from Frank McCollam’s published book of tunes. The tune above, in all it’s versions, is what McCollam called THE GRANNY ROCK.
